chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a Muslim man who has a Jewish or Christian wife, or a female slave whom he has freed, and he disowns her child and accuses her (of adultery). Is there li'an upon him? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.لِعَانٌ: Li'an (mutual imprecation), a specific legal procedure in Islamic jurisprudence where a husband accuses his wife of adultery without witnesses, and both swear oaths to curse each other if lying.
key_terms.نَفَى وَلَدَهَا: He disowned his child from her.

ai.seo_question: Does li'an apply to a Muslim man married to a non-Muslim woman if he disowns her child?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim, the specific legal nuance of li'an is clarified for interfaith or slave marriages, where the ritual of mutual imprecation is deemed inapplicable. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential treatment of non-Muslim wives (Ahl al-Kitab) and freed slaves within Shia fiqh, distinguishing their marital dissolution mechanics from those of Muslim women. The absence of li'an here underscores the principle that the specific evidentiary ritual is tied to the particularities of the marital bond in these contexts.
